title: [Shortcut Guide] Crashes when pressing any Win+number taskbar shortcut while the guide is open
author: kmhaugen
summary: Shortcut Guide has a concrete crash repro when Win+number is pressed while taskbar indicators are showing, and the next useful step is a maintainer-side debugger repro against the taskbar-indicator path.

judgment.rationale: The issue already provides exact steps, says the crash happens on every tested Win+number shortcut, and includes crash-dump symptom details, so a reporter-facing info request would add less value than a direct local repro.
evidence: The reporter gives a four-step repro and says every tested Win+number taskbar shortcut triggers the crash while Shortcut Guide is open.
The crash produces a user-mode dump and reports exception code 0xC0000005 in PowerToys.ShortcutGuide.exe.
Current Shortcut Guide activation code shows a dedicated ShowTaskbarIndicators path that displays taskbar indicators while the Windows key remains active.
TasklistPositions.GetButtons() marshals a native taskbar-button buffer into managed structures during the same taskbar-indicator flow.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce the Win+number taskbar-indicator crash on current main and inspect the native taskbar-button ownership and overlay close path under a debugger.

fix_assessment.rationale: This is a concrete Shortcut Guide crash with a narrow module area, but the exact stale-pointer or re-entrancy site still needs maintainer-side debugging.

issue_context.summary: Pressing any Win+number taskbar shortcut while Shortcut Guide is showing taskbar indicators reliably crashes the Shortcut Guide process with an access violation.
known_information: The issue provides exact reproduction steps and says the crash is fully reproducible.
The selected taskbar app still activates, which means the Windows shortcut succeeds even though Shortcut Guide crashes afterward.
The report includes exception code 0xC0000005 and two top-of-stack signatures from dump analysis.
No assignee, linked fix, or maintainer discussion is visible.
inferences: The crash is likely inside the taskbar-indicator overlay maintenance path rather than in the actual Windows taskbar activation behavior.
Because the target app activates successfully, the bug probably happens during or immediately after Shortcut Guide reacts to the taskbar state change.
issue_context.analysis: This is best represented as reproducible. The public report already contains enough to justify maintainer-side debugger work without asking the reporter for a new generic information package.
initial_investigation: src/modules/ShortcutGuide/ShortcutGuide.Ui/ShortcutGuideXAML/App.xaml.cs has a dedicated ShowTaskbarIndicators activation path that captures the foreground window and immediately updates the taskbar pane.

src/modules/ShortcutGuide/ShortcutGuide.Ui/Helpers/TasklistPositions.cs marshals a native GetTasklistButtons buffer into managed TasklistButton structs, which is a plausible crash boundary when the underlying taskbar state changes under Win+number.

src/modules/ShortcutGuide/ShortcutGuide.Ui/ShortcutGuideXAML/Controls/TaskbarPaneControl.xaml.cs rebuilds visual indicators directly from that native taskbar-button data each time the pane is updated.

actions.label: Approve Shortcut Guide Win+number crash investigation
actions.note: The crash path is narrow, but the proposed root cause remains low-confidence until a debugger identifies the exact faulting transition.

actions.label: Reproduce Shortcut Guide Win+number crash
actions.note: Drive the exact taskbar-indicator flow under a debugger and capture the faulting frame when the target app activates.

prerequisites: Use a build where Shortcut Guide can show Win+number taskbar indicators.
Open enough taskbar-pinned or running apps that the taskbar indicators are visible.
steps: Keep it open until the Win+1, Win+2, Win+3, and similar taskbar indicators are displayed above the taskbar icons.
Press one of the corresponding Win+number shortcuts while the guide is still visible.
Observe whether the target app activates and whether PowerToys.ShortcutGuide.exe crashes immediately afterward.
reproduce.expected_result: The taskbar app should activate and Shortcut Guide should close or refresh cleanly without crashing the Shortcut Guide process.

proposed_fixes.title: Stabilize Shortcut Guide taskbar-indicator teardown during Win+number activation
proposed_fixes.root_cause: When the taskbar-indicator surface is open, Win+number changes the foreground window and taskbar state while Shortcut Guide is still reading and rendering native taskbar-button data, which likely leaves a stale native buffer or re-entrant close/update path that causes the access violation.
plan: Reproduce the issue under a debugger on current main and capture the faulting frame during Win+number activation.

Audit the ShowTaskbarIndicators -> UpdateTaskbarPaneLayout -> TasklistPositions.GetButtons flow for stale taskbar-button memory, re-entrant close behavior, or layout refresh after the overlay should already be closing.

Guard buffer lifetime and skip or cancel taskbar-pane updates once activation closes or invalidates the overlay, then add a regression or manual validation scenario for Win+number while the guide is open.
verification: Open Shortcut Guide until taskbar indicators are shown, press Win+1 through Win+9, and confirm the selected taskbar app activates without crashing PowerToys.ShortcutGuide.exe.
Repeat with taskbar indicators opening and closing multiple times to confirm the fix is robust across repeated activations.

confidence.rationale: The failing path is tightly scoped, but the public crash data is still too shallow to prove whether the fault is stale native memory, re-entrancy, or another taskbar-indicator teardown bug.
